memory_update.text: ESI should be tracked as the most size-filter-compatible US-listed specialty-chemistry candidate for IC substrates, copper adhesion, RDL, copper pillar, TSV, and wafer-level packaging materials.

MKSI should be tracked as a larger but still relevant Atotech-enabled process chemistry/equipment candidate for package substrate manufacturing, copper activation, metallization, plating, and laser drilling.
ONTO should be tracked as an advanced-packaging yield-control equipment candidate tied to HBM, package inspection, 3D metrology, lithography, and factory analytics.

US-listed pure-play ABF substrate exposure appears limited; the investable US universe for this node is more likely in adjacent wet chemistry, metallization, inspection/metrology, process-control software, and OSAT pull-through.

PDF Solutions (PDFS) was not included due to the four-candidate limit, but remains a watch-list candidate for process data, yield analytics, and semiconductor supply-chain orchestration across fabless, foundry, OSAT, and test operations.

node: Advanced packaging substrates, ABF-style insulating materials, and copper-bonding chemistry
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the US-listed universe around the advanced-packaging substrate/materials chokepoint. The strongest US-listed discovery candidates are not true ABF substrate makers; rather, they sit in copper plating, adhesion, wet chemistry, inspection/metrology, and process-control layers that can affect package substrate yield and advanced-packaging ramp speed. Element Solutions and MKS/Atotech are the most directly tied to copper chemistry and IC substrate process materials. Onto Innovation is a yield-control equipment candidate for HBM and advanced packaging. Amkor is included as a reference/context anchor because it is a US-listed advanced-packaging OSAT whose capacity expansion may pull demand for substrates, chemistry, metrology, and process control.
